title: Chozodia searchlights, security lasers and searchlight eyes
divergences: Searchlights are drawn opaque and above the backgrounds (natively they flicker behind BG1 with draw order 1), the BG0 transparency fades (PrimarySpriteB3, the security lasers' TransparencySpriteUpdateBldalpha; their fade state is kept in work2/work3) and sounds are not reproduced; missiles hitting an immune sprite are removed instead of tumbling.
notes: Searchlights sweep diagonally half a pixel a frame between stop-enemy blocks, flickering, and ring the alarm on contact (SSC_CHECK_COLLIDING), then hold it; security lasers size themselves 2 to 5 blocks to the first block above or right, and when tripped mark the Space Pirates, fade out and hold the alarm; searchlight eyes (immune to projectiles until the Fully Powered Suit, SP_IMMUNE_TO_PROJECTILES with the invincible impact) move along their wall, cast a seven-block beam that rings the alarm unless a wall shields Samus, then shoot projectiles (16 damage) every 1.5 seconds. Checked in chozodia_003 (a tripped laser releases the waiting pirates), chozodia_016 and chozodia_030.
next_action: Port the security gates and the event spritesets that place these systems.

title: Dessgeegas and the Long Beam Dessgeega
divergences: Freezing, the sounds and the screen shakes are not ported; door locks are only reported (gDoorUnlockTimer is not consumed by the runtime) and removed floor blocks keep their background graphics; nothing sets EVENT_VIEWED_STATUE_ROOM yet and the event spriteset that places the Long Beam Dessgeega is not exported, so that variant only runs in tests.
notes: Ground and ceiling Dessgeegas share the Sidehopper state machine with their own tables and sizes; every ground Dessgeega death sets the Long Beam event and unlocks the doors (the game's bug, kept). The Long Beam variant checks its events, locks the doors, waits hidden from Samus and projectiles, drops through the floor removing three blocks with dust and debris, and lands on the next one.
next_action: Export the event spritesets and port the statue room event and the door lock lifecycle.

title: Space Pirates and their lasers
divergences: SpawnWaitingPirates reads the room's default spriteset only (event spritesets are not exported) and runs on door transitions, not on the debug teleport; the alarm music, palette animation and sounds, freezing (only the laser check runs while frozen), the stun palette as drawn colours and the laser's draw order and BG priority are not reproduced; the Space Pirate carrying a power bomb, the black and escape-ship pirates are not ported; the runtime keeps the alarm across room loads without SpriteLoadAllData's new-game reset.
notes: The five SpacePirate sprites (normal, three waiting, the faster-shooting variant) and SSPRITE_SPACE_PIRATE_LASER: line-of-sight detection on the clipdata grid (forward rows, diagonals up and down, crawling and climbing cases) through the gSpriteDrawOrder scratch flags, walking with acceleration and slope slowdown, the obstacle probes (jumps from the four ROM tables, crawling under low ceilings, turns), zonelines and wall jump points from the exported clipdata movement (M lines), climbing, wall pauses, wall jumps, crawling, alerted walking, charging and two-laser volleys on the ground and on walls, lasers hurting Samus and other pirates, the Chozodia alarm timer (set on sight, 480 frames, stopped by the last pirate's death, kept after Mecha Ridley) and the laser's CAA_BOMB_PISTOL on hatches. With the alarm on (or Mecha Ridley dead), every door transition spawns a waiting pirate at the arrival point (half a block back toward the door; graphics slot 5 in spritesets 88 and 103; crawling out of hatchless doors), and a room whose spriteset has no pirate stops the alarm. Rooms export their default spriteset (S lines). Smoke-run in the 47 Chozodia rooms with pirates.
next_action: Port the power-bomb, black and escape-ship pirates and the security systems that ring the alarm (searchlights, security lasers); resolve the event spritesets.

title: Room backgrounds: layers, priorities, BG0 blend and BG3 scrolling
divergences: Animated tilesets and palettes, the mother ship common tiles, BG2 movement (BG_PROP_MOVING), BG0 movement (water, clouds, snow), BG2/BG3 gradient effects, windows and screen fades are not reproduced; BG2 and the LZ77 BG0 scroll with BG1; the camera is the runtime's 320x224 follow view, not the native scrolling; particles share the sprites' priority.
notes: VRAM and BG palette RAM are rebuilt as RoomLoadTileset leaves them (common tiles at 0x4800, tileset at 0x5800, background graphics below 0xFDE0, palette rows 0-2 common and 3-15 from the tileset); every tileset gets a sheet of its 1024 metatiles and the 208 common ones, rooms export their BG0 (RLE), BG1 and BG2 block maps and their BG3 / LZ77 BG0 text maps; the runtime draws them by the native priorities of the room's transparency value (Samus and sprites at priority 2, or 1 on top of the backgrounds), blends BG0 (additive at EVA/16 or alpha at 16 - EVB) and scrolls BG3 with ScrollBg3 including rooms starting from the bottom. Checked in brinstar_000, chozodia_016 and norfair_005 captures.
next_action: Animated tiles and palettes, then BG movement effects.
